nodes.label: Procurement
nodes.title: Procurement
nodes.summary: The enterprise procurement process framework. Twenty-five processes across six domains, expressed as text-first process objects that are versioned in Git, published through the management system, and served to AI agents over MCP with explicit delegation boundaries.

data.title: Procurement
data.summary: The enterprise procurement process framework. Twenty-five processes across six domains, expressed as text-first process objects that are versioned in Git, published through the management system, and served to AI agents over MCP with explicit delegation boundaries.

nodes.label: Strategy and Performance
nodes.title: Strategy and Performance
nodes.summary: Aligns procurement with enterprise strategy, manages risk, measures performance, controls the savings funnel and owns sustainability governance across the procurement portfolio.

data.title: Strategy and Performance
data.summary: Aligns procurement with enterprise strategy, manages risk, measures performance, controls the savings funnel and owns sustainability governance across the procurement portfolio.

steps.title: Collect enterprise objectives and demand signals
steps.notes: The agent extracts objectives verbatim with citations. It does not interpret ambition into a number — that is a human judgement that must be traceable to the objective.

steps.title: Build the procurement portfolio view
steps.notes: Concentration, tail spend, maverick-spend and category volatility are computed here. Findings feed the category boundaries, not the strategy itself.

steps.title: Define category boundaries and taxonomy
steps.notes: Boundary changes are the highest-consequence decision in this step: they move spend between categories and therefore between owners. Every proposed change is listed with the spend that would move.

steps.title: Draft the procurement strategy
Co-design review with practitioners
steps.notes: This is the community step. Practitioners from each domain review whether the strategy is executable with the tools and levers they actually have. Unresolved practitioner objections are recorded in the approval record, not silently dropped.

steps.title: Approve and publish
Enrol into the management system and notify

kpis.name: Spend under management
kpis.definition: Share of total addressable spend governed by an approved category strategy

kpis.name: Strategy-to-execution alignment
kpis.definition: Share of sourcing events traceable to an approved category strategy lever

steps.title: Profile the category spend and demand
Analyse the supplier base and market structure
Determine sourcing levers and sequence them
steps.notes: Levers are ranked by value, effort and time-to-benefit. The agent may propose and rank; the sequence is a human decision because it consumes organisational change capacity.

steps.title: Build the savings plan and negotiation calendar
Assess risk and ESG profile for the category
Co-design with the category team and business sponsors
Validate savings with finance and approve

kpis.name: Strategy currency
kpis.definition: Share of categories with a strategy reviewed within the last 12 months

kpis.name: Lever conversion
kpis.definition: Share of planned sourcing levers that have been executed within the plan year

steps.title: Identify risks from spend, supplier and incident data
Score likelihood and impact against the published methodology
steps.notes: The agent applies the published scoring matrix and shows its working. It never assigns a rating the methodology does not produce from the supplied evidence.

steps.title: Define mitigation actions, owners and funding
Escalate high-rated and accepted risks
outputs: Escalations to the Delegation Review Board
steps.notes: Risk acceptance is always a named human decision. The agent prepares the escalation pack, it does not accept risk.

steps.title: Review, report and refresh the register

kpis.name: Risk closure
kpis.definition: Share of high-rated risks closed within the agreed remediation window

kpis.name: Overdue mitigations
kpis.definition: Count of mitigation actions past their due date

outputs.name: Escalations to the Delegation Review Board

steps.title: Collect performance, exception and agent telemetry
Identify improvement candidates
Prioritise by value, effort and risk reduction
Design the change across process, skill, policy and template
steps.notes: A change is only complete when it names every artefact it touches. A change to a step without its skill, policy or template is incomplete and the validator rejects it.

steps.title: Validate through a pilot
Publish the framework release
steps.notes: Publication is a merge to the main branch after review — the same co-design governance that governs content applies to the framework itself.

steps.title: Measure and report realised benefit

kpis.name: Cycle time reduction
kpis.definition: Weighted average reduction in end-to-end process cycle time year on year

kpis.name: Exception rate
kpis.definition: Invoices and POs requiring manual exception handling, as a share of volume

kpis.name: Framework change lead time
kpis.definition: Working days from improvement proposal to published release

steps.title: Confirm the finance-validated baseline
Capture opportunities into the pipeline with stage evidence
steps.notes: An entry without evidence for its stage is rejected. "Identified" requires a benchmark; "validated" requires finance; "realised" requires post-award spend.

steps.title: Validate each stage with finance
Track realisation against post-award spend
Analyse leakage and report

kpis.name: Realisation rate
kpis.definition: Finance-validated realised savings ÷ savings forecast at the start of the cycle

kpis.name: Leakage rate
kpis.definition: Value lost between funnel stages ÷ value entering the funnel

steps.title: Build and maintain the renewal calendar
Benchmark current pricing against the market
steps.notes: Every benchmark used must be traceable to a source and a date. An agent that cannot cite a benchmark must say so rather than estimate.

steps.title: Prepare the re-negotiation position and ask
Execute the negotiation
steps.notes: Conceding position is a human act. The agent may prepare data, simulate counter-positions and summarise, but the conversation itself is a human negotiation.

steps.title: Execute the amendment and capture the price-down
outputs: Executed price amendment or new agreement

steps.title: Propagate the new pricing to transactional systems

kpis.name: Re-negotiation coverage
kpis.definition: Share of contracts reaching notice window that were actively re-negotiated

kpis.name: Price-down captured
kpis.definition: Value captured through re-negotiation as a share of renewed contract value

outputs.name: Executed price amendment or new agreement

steps.title: Translate ESG targets into supplier expectations
Collect supplier ESG data
Assess and score supplier ESG performance
steps.notes: Self-declared data is scored as self-declared. The scorecard records provenance for every data point — this distinction is the whole point of the exercise.

steps.title: Embed ESG criteria into sourcing and contracting
outputs: ESG criteria in sourcing and contracts

steps.title: Verify material claims and raise findings
Produce the ESG disclosure data pack

kpis.name: Spend with assessed ESG data
kpis.definition: Share of addressable spend where the supplier has current ESG data

kpis.name: Verified claims
kpis.definition: Share of material supplier ESG claims independently verified

outputs.name: ESG criteria in sourcing and contracts

nodes.label: Intake Management
nodes.title: Intake Management
nodes.summary: Captures every demand for goods and services at the point of origin, qualifies it against strategy and budget, and routes it to the right buying channel — so that only valid, funded, approved requests reach sourcing.

data.title: Intake Management
data.summary: Captures every demand for goods and services at the point of origin, qualifies it against strategy and budget, and routes it to the right buying channel — so that only valid, funded, approved requests reach sourcing.

steps.title: Capture the requirement through guided intake
steps.notes: An assistant may conduct the conversation and pre-fill the form, but every field it fills is marked as agent-sourced and the requester confirms them. It never fabricates a justification.

steps.title: Classify the request into category and subcategory
Match against catalogue and contract supply
steps.notes: The agent explains the match — which catalogue item, on what attribute — because an unexplained match is indistinguishable from a guess to the requester.

steps.title: Qualify against strategy, budget and thresholds
steps.notes: Budget and threshold checks are blocking: the agent cannot pass a request that breaches policy, and it cannot approve its own request.

steps.title: Consolidate and de-duplicate against open demand
Route to the buying channel

decision_space.escalation_band: value above auto_route_value_eur

steps.notes: Below the catalogue threshold the agent may route directly to a purchase order. Above it, or where the agent judges the match weak, the routing escalates to a buyer with its reasoning attached.

steps.title: Inform the requester of the outcome

decision_space.escalation_band: above auto_route_value_eur, or when the routing rule cannot be resolved uniquely

mandate.title: Straight-through routing of qualified requests
mandate.rationale: Routing a qualified request to the buying channel is a rule, not a judgement: the channel strategy, the category tree and the threshold matrix determine the destination. The human value is in qualifying the request, not in pressing a button.

kpis.name: Catalogue hit rate
kpis.definition: Share of requests resolved from an approved catalogue item

kpis.name: Time to first response
kpis.definition: Elapsed working hours from request submission to a routing decision or clarification request

kpis.name: Straight-through qualification
kpis.definition: Share of requests qualified without buyer intervention

steps.title: Collect and normalise demand signals
Detect duplication and fragmentation
Consolidate requests into aggregation groups
steps.notes: Requests belonging to different budget holders are never merged without each holder's consent — consolidation must not become a way of removing someone's visibility of their own spend.

steps.title: Analyse demand patterns and forecast
Shape demand with requesters and standardise where possible
Publish the consolidated demand plan

decision_space.escalation_band: variance above tolerance
plan variance against the previous cycle above the published tolerance

mandate.title: Publication of the consolidated demand plan
mandate.rationale: Consolidation is deterministic once the aggregation groups and the de-duplication rules are set. The plan is an internal planning artefact, fully reversible, and every figure traces back to the requests it aggregates.

kpis.name: Aggregation rate
kpis.definition: Share of requests that enter sourcing as part of an aggregated event

kpis.name: Duplication rate
kpis.definition: Duplicate requests identified as a share of total requests

nodes.label: Source to Contract
nodes.title: Source to Contract
nodes.summary: Runs the competitive process from requirement analysis through sourcing event, award decision and contract formation — with the strategy, policies and evaluation criteria declared up front and enforced in real time.

data.title: Source to Contract
data.summary: Runs the competitive process from requirement analysis through sourcing event, award decision and contract formation — with the strategy, policies and evaluation criteria declared up front and enforced in real time.

steps.title: Analyse the requirement and define the evaluation criteria
steps.notes: Criteria are drafted here, before any supplier is approached. This is the structural defence against post-hoc criteria drift.

steps.title: Perform supplier market analysis
steps.notes: The agent may research the public market and summarise internal performance data. It may not include a supplier that has not passed due diligence, and it may not rank suppliers before the strategy is approved.

steps.title: Determine sourcing strategy and event type
steps.notes: Competitive tender, RFQ, e-auction, dynamic sourcing or single source. A single-source recommendation must carry a written justification that is approved at award level.

steps.title: Build and approve the supplier shortlist
Draft the RFx package from the approved template
steps.notes: The agent fills only fields declared fillable in the template. Commercial terms and legal text are locked — it proposes, it does not write the contract.

steps.title: Internal review and approval of the event
Publish the event
steps.notes: Publication is externally visible and irreversible in substance. This is a hard control point: the agent may prepare and may even execute publication once approved, but the approval is never the agent's own.

steps.title: Manage clarifications and addenda
steps.notes: Clarifications go to all participants, never to one. An agent that discovers a question is commercially sensitive raises it to a human rather than answering it.

kpis.name: Time to publish
kpis.definition: Working days from approved strategy to published event

kpis.name: Competitive participation
kpis.definition: Share of published events receiving more than one bid

kpis.name: Shortlist quality
kpis.definition: Share of shortlisted suppliers that respond with a valid bid

steps.title: Receive bids and run compliance screening
steps.notes: Non-compliance is established against the published requirements only. A bid is never screened against criteria introduced after publication.

steps.title: Evaluate bids against the locked criteria
steps.notes: The agent computes weighted scores and drafts rationales from the stated criteria. Every score it produces carries the evidence that produced it, so a human reviewer can disagree with the reasoning rather than guess at it.

steps.title: Consolidate panel scores and resolve divergence
steps.notes: Divergence between evaluators is surfaced, not averaged away silently. The agent flags the criteria where evaluators disagree most, which is usually where the requirement was ambiguous.

steps.title: Run clarification and negotiation rounds
Produce the award recommendation
steps.notes: The recommendation names the supplier, the price, the score, the rationale and every exception taken. A recommendation that needs a paragraph of explanation is a recommendation that is not ready.

steps.title: Approve the award decision
Notify bidders and communicate the outcome
Record the award and the savings entry

kpis.name: Time to award
kpis.definition: Working days from event close to award approval

kpis.name: Evaluation coverage
kpis.definition: Share of bids scored against every locked criterion

kpis.name: Award justification completeness
kpis.definition: Share of award records with complete rationale and approvals

steps.title: Select the contract type and template
Draft the contract from the template and award terms
steps.notes: The agent fills the declared fillable fields and populates the commercial schedule from the award. It does not alter legal clauses — anything it cannot fill, it raises.

steps.title: Legal and commercial review
steps.notes: The agent can flag clauses that deviate from the playbook and summarise the commercial risk. It cannot resolve a legal deviation.

steps.title: Negotiate with the supplier
steps.notes: Position and concession are human acts. The agent prepares a position summary and a fallback playbook before the conversation.

steps.title: Final approval and signature
Activate the contract and register obligations
steps.notes: Obligation extraction is high-value automation: dates, notice periods, price escalators and service levels are read from the executed text into a register that drives renewal reminders and risk checks.

kpis.name: Time to signature
kpis.definition: Working days from award approval to executed contract

kpis.name: Template adherence
kpis.definition: Share of contracts executed without a non-standard clause

kpis.name: Obligation coverage
kpis.definition: Share of executed contracts with a complete obligation register

steps.title: Specify the material and its classification
Search for an existing equivalent material
steps.notes: Reuse before create. A new material where an existing one fits is the single most common source of spend fragmentation.

steps.title: Create or enrich the material master record

decision_space.escalation_band: fields not derivable from the request

steps.title: Validate completeness against the required-field standard
Declare the receipt path with supply chain
steps.notes: Who creates the inventory receipt, who confirms quantity, who owns variance — this is recorded once, explicitly, on the material record, and referenced by Proc_4.3.

steps.title: Govern material master changes

decision_space.escalation_band: change to a field that is under a current governance freeze
any field that cannot be derived from the request or the standard catalogue

mandate.title: Material master creation and change governance
mandate.rationale: Material master creation is a field-level transformation against a published required-field standard. Errors are detected by the same standard that created them, and every change is reversible and logged.

kpis.name: Material master completeness
kpis.definition: Share of active material records complete against the required-field standard

kpis.name: Duplicate rate
kpis.definition: Duplicate material records detected per 100 creations

kpis.name: Receipt reconciliation rate
kpis.definition: Share of receipts matched between purchase receipt and inventory receipt without manual intervention

steps.title: Detect a new or changed award or contract
Extract commercial terms
steps.notes: Price, unit of measure, currency, payment terms, validity period, tolerances, service levels, rebate and escalation clauses. Every extracted value carries a confidence and a source reference; anything below threshold is sent to a human rather than published.

steps.title: Map terms to catalogue, item and supplier records
Generate validation and matching rules
steps.notes: Rules are versioned and reversible. A rule that would reject legitimate orders is a finding for Proc_1.4, not a licence to relax it.

steps.title: Publish to the transactional systems
Reconcile and report completeness
steps.notes: The report lists contracts not yet enriched and terms published but not matched. This is the main input to the improvement loop in Proc_1.4.

kpis.name: Enrichment coverage
kpis.definition: Share of active contracts whose commercial terms are reflected in transactional master data

kpis.name: First-time-right match rate
kpis.definition: Share of invoices matched automatically on first submission

kpis.name: Enrichment latency
kpis.definition: Working hours from contract execution to transactional publication

nodes.label: Purchase Requisition to Purchase Order
nodes.title: Purchase Requisition to Purchase Order
nodes.summary: Turns an approved requisition into a valid purchase order: verifies budget, obtains the right approvals, applies contract pricing, and issues the order with complete and accurate data.

data.title: Purchase Requisition to Purchase Order
data.summary: Turns an approved requisition into a valid purchase order: verifies budget, obtains the right approvals, applies contract pricing, and issues the order with complete and accurate data.

steps.title: Validate requisition completeness

decision_space.escalation_band: mandatory field missing and not derivable from the request

steps.notes: The agent returns the requisition to the requester with the specific missing fields. It does not fill a missing business justification or cost centre — those are facts only the requester holds.

steps.title: Verify budget availability and apply the encumbrance
Check contract coverage and price correctness
steps.notes: A non-covered requisition is not rejected outright — it is routed to the sourcing or exception path with the value gap quantified. That is how contract coverage improves rather than merely being enforced.

steps.title: Detect split requests against related open requisitions
Route for approval per the threshold matrix

decision_space.escalation_band: above auto_release_value_eur

steps.notes: Delegation chains are resolved by the routing engine, not by the agent. An agent may not approve where the human approver is the requester or the preparer.

steps.title: Approve or reject
Release for purchase order creation

decision_space.escalation_band: no valid approval reference on the requisition
above auto_release_value_eur, any suspected split, or a failed budget check

mandate.title: Straight-through requisition validation, routing and release
mandate.rationale: The requisition is the highest-volume entry point in procurement and the place where information chasing starts. Completeness checking, budget verification and threshold routing are rule-bound, fully auditable and reversible. Below the auto-release threshold the process becomes straight-through — a human only sees what the rules could not decide.

kpis.name: Requisition approval cycle time
kpis.definition: Elapsed working hours from qualified requisition to approval

kpis.name: Straight-through approval rate
kpis.definition: Share of requisitions approved without buyer intervention

kpis.name: Requisition rejection rate
kpis.definition: Requisitions returned for correction as a share of submitted

steps.title: Validate supplier, item and pricing data
Apply contract pricing and commercial terms
steps.notes: Price deviations inside tolerance are applied automatically; outside tolerance the PO is staged and escalated with the variance quantified.

steps.title: Build the purchase order
Validate the PO for completeness and policy compliance
steps.notes: Completeness here means the fields a supplier needs to act without a phone call: address, contact, delivery date, unit of measure, price, currency, payment terms and tax treatment.

steps.title: Obtain approval where the threshold requires it
Issue and transmit the purchase order

decision_space.escalation_band: value above auto_issue_value_eur

steps.notes: Below the delegated threshold the agent issues without a human seeing the order — provided every blocking validation passed. Above it, the order waits for a named human.

steps.title: Monitor acknowledgement and chase non-acknowledgement

decision_space.escalation_band: above auto_issue_value_eur, or any price variance above the contract price

mandate.title: Issue of a purchase order inside the delegated authority
mandate.rationale: Once a purchase order has been approved and passes policy validation, transmitting it to a supplier is mechanical. The residual risk is wrong pricing or an unauthorised buyer, both of which are caught by the pre-flight checks and are reversible by issuing a change order.

kpis.name: PO first-time-right
kpis.definition: Share of issued POs requiring no correction, amendment or rejection

kpis.name: Requisition to PO cycle time
kpis.definition: Elapsed working hours from released requisition to PO issue

kpis.name: Contract-covered PO rate
kpis.definition: Share of issued POs priced against an active contract

kpis.name: Supplier acknowledgement rate
kpis.definition: Share of issued POs acknowledged by the supplier within the agreed window

steps.title: Confirm the delivery expectation and prepare the receipt
Receive and inspect the delivery
steps.notes: Physical verification is irreducibly human. The agent may guide the check against a quality checklist, but it never records a receipt for goods nobody has seen.

steps.title: Record the receipt in the transactional system

decision_space.escalation_band: quantity or price variance

steps.title: Resolve variances, damage and rejections
steps.notes: Partial receipts, over-receipts, damages and quality failures are classified, costed and routed. The agent builds the claim; the buyer negotiates it.

steps.title: Coordinate inventory posting with supply chain
Complete the purchase order lines

decision_space.escalation_band: an open dispute on the line
any quantity or price variance, or a receipt against a closed order line

mandate.title: Goods receipt posting and purchase order completion
mandate.rationale: Posting a receipt against an open purchase order line is a lookup, not a judgement. The quantity and condition come from the delivery, the price from the order. A wrong posting is corrected by a reversal with the same audit trail.

kpis.name: Receipt accuracy
kpis.definition: Share of receipts recorded with no subsequent quantity or value correction

kpis.name: Receipt timeliness
kpis.definition: Elapsed time from physical arrival to system receipt, in hours

kpis.name: Three-way match readiness
kpis.definition: Share of invoices matched on first submission

nodes.label: Invoice to Pay
nodes.title: Invoice to Pay
nodes.summary: Receives supplier invoices, matches them against the purchase order and receipt, resolves exceptions, and releases payment — with a proportionate, always-on control against duplicate and fraudulent payment.

data.title: Invoice to Pay
data.summary: Receives supplier invoices, matches them against the purchase order and receipt, resolves exceptions, and releases payment — with a proportionate, always-on control against duplicate and fraudulent payment.

steps.title: Capture the invoice from the source channel
Validate structure, tax and mandatory fields
Screen for duplicates
steps.notes: Probabilistic matching catches the near-duplicates — same invoice, different reference number — that exact matching misses. A hold is a hold until a human clears it.

steps.title: Screen for fraud, bank changes and sanctions exposure
steps.notes: A recent bank-detail change plus an invoice above a value threshold is the classic payment-redirection pattern. It is flagged on the combination, not on either signal alone.

steps.title: Route to matching

kpis.name: Auto-capture rate
kpis.definition: Share of invoices captured without manual keying

kpis.name: Duplicate rate
kpis.definition: Duplicate invoices caught before payment, per 1,000 invoices

kpis.name: Invoice completeness
kpis.definition: Share of invoices passing structural validation on first submission

steps.title: Match the invoice against the purchase order

decision_space.escalation_band: price variance above tolerance

steps.title: Match against the goods receipt or service acceptance

decision_space.escalation_band: no goods receipt or service acceptance found

steps.title: Evaluate variances against the tolerance rules

decision_space.escalation_band: variance above tolerance

steps.notes: A variance inside tolerance passes. A variance outside tolerance produces an exception with the specific breach named — which price, which quantity, which term — not a generic "match failed".

steps.title: Route for approval per the threshold matrix
Approve for payment
Release into the payment run or route to exceptions

decision_space.escalation_band: any variance above tolerance, or a missing receipt

mandate.title: Three-way match execution
mandate.rationale: The match itself is arithmetic: invoice against order, invoice against receipt, variance against tolerance. A machine does it faster and more consistently than a person, and the three-way match has been the standard control since the 1960s. The approval and the payment release stay human.

kpis.name: Straight-through processing rate
kpis.definition: Share of invoices matched and approved without any human touch

kpis.name: Match pass rate
kpis.definition: Share of invoices matched without variance

kpis.name: Invoice to approval time
kpis.definition: Elapsed working hours from invoice receipt to payment approval

steps.title: Classify the exception and identify the likely cause
steps.notes: Classification is the highest-value automated step in accounts payable. It decides who owns the exception — and therefore how long it takes — before anyone reads it.

steps.title: Assign ownership and package the context
steps.notes: The package is what the owner actually needs: the invoice, the PO, the receipt, the contract clause, the discrepancy, and what has already been tried.

steps.title: Investigate and gather evidence
Resolve the exception
steps.notes: Correct the record, dispute the invoice, write it off, or cancel it. The agent prepares each option with its commercial consequence; the decision is always human.

steps.title: Re-process and release
Capture the root cause for process improvement

kpis.name: Exception resolution time
kpis.definition: Elapsed working days from exception raised to resolved

kpis.name: First-time-right resolution rate
kpis.definition: Share of exceptions resolved without rework

kpis.name: Recurring exception rate
kpis.definition: Share of exceptions matching a previously identified root cause

inputs.name: Invoice, PO, receipt and contract records

steps.title: Schedule invoices into the payment run
steps.notes: The agent optimises the run against discount deadlines, cash position and payment terms, and explains the schedule it produced.

steps.title: Verify supplier banking data independently
steps.notes: Verification must be independent of the channel the change request arrived on — a callback to a known contact number, never a number from the change request itself. This single control defeats the most common procurement fraud.

steps.title: Review and approve the payment run
Release the payment file
Send remittance advice and reconcile

kpis.name: On-time payment rate
kpis.definition: Share of invoices paid within contractual payment terms

kpis.name: Early-payment discount captured
kpis.definition: Value of discounts captured divided by discounts available

kpis.name: Payment error rate
kpis.definition: Payment runs requiring recall or correction, per 1,000 payments

nodes.label: Supplier Management
nodes.title: Supplier Management
nodes.summary: Owns the supplier lifecycle — onboarding into systems, qualification, performance management and offboarding — and the master data that every other procurement process depends on.

data.title: Supplier Management
data.summary: Owns the supplier lifecycle — onboarding into systems, qualification, performance management and offboarding — and the master data that every other procurement process depends on.

steps.title: Receive the application and check for an existing record
steps.notes: Duplicate detection here prevents the classic failure: the same supplier existing as two records with two bank accounts, one of which is stale.

steps.title: Run due diligence and screening
steps.notes: A sanctions hit is a hard stop. The agent escalates; it never downgrades a screening outcome on its own judgement.

steps.title: Validate the commercial and tax data
Verify banking details independently
Create the supplier master record
Approve and activate to transactable status
Communicate onboarding outcome and next steps to the supplier

kpis.name: Onboarding lead time
kpis.definition: Elapsed working days from application to transactable status

kpis.name: First-time-right onboarding
kpis.definition: Share of suppliers activated without a master data correction afterwards

kpis.name: Due diligence completeness
kpis.definition: Share of active suppliers with a current, complete due diligence pack

inputs.name: Financial and compliance due diligence data

steps.title: Confirm the qualification criteria in scope
Collect and validate the evidence
steps.notes: Evidence has a validity date. An expired certificate is treated as absent, and the agent says so plainly rather than scoring it as a pass.

steps.title: Score against the criteria
Decide: approve, conditionally approve or decline

decision_space.escalation_band: score within 10% of a band boundary

steps.title: Set the re-qualification schedule and conditions

decision_space.escalation_band: total score within 10% of a band boundary, or a missing mandatory certificate

mandate.title: Bounded supplier qualification decision
mandate.rationale: The qualification outcome is a choice from a closed set — approve, conditionally approve, decline — driven by a published scoring scale. The judgement is bounded, the candidate set is closed and the outcome is fully auditable, which is the definition of a delegable decision.

kpis.name: Qualification coverage
kpis.definition: Share of suppliers transacting against a category with a current qualification

kpis.name: Qualification lead time
kpis.definition: Working days from request to decision

steps.title: Detect and confirm the offboarding trigger
Block transactional status immediately
steps.notes: Blocking comes first and is irreversible in the session. Resolving the remaining exposure — payments, data, access — takes days; a supplier that can transact during those days is a supplier that can be paid for goods never delivered.

steps.title: Inventory and resolve open commitments
Revoke access and determine the data disposition
steps.notes: Retention obligations override the default of deletion. The agent flags every record under legal or contractual hold and marks it undeletable.

steps.title: Notify the supplier and close the relationship
Attest completion and archive the record

kpis.name: Offboarding completion rate
kpis.definition: Share of triggered offboardings completed within the target window

kpis.name: Post-termination transactions
kpis.definition: Count of transactions with a terminated supplier after termination date

steps.title: Define the scorecard and the measurement method
Collect and normalise performance data
Score performance and identify trends
steps.notes: Trend matters more than the point score. A supplier at 88% and falling is a different conversation from one at 88% and rising, and the scorecard shows both.

steps.title: Hold the performance review with the supplier
Agree development or corrective action
outputs: Development plan or corrective action plan

steps.title: Feed performance into strategy and renewal decisions

kpis.name: Performance review coverage
kpis.definition: Share of strategic suppliers with a current scorecard and review

kpis.name: Service level attainment
kpis.definition: Weighted average attainment of contracted service levels across the supplier base

kpis.name: Corrective action closure
kpis.definition: Share of corrective actions closed within the agreed window

outputs.name: Development plan or corrective action plan

nodes.label: AI Delegation Matrix
nodes.title: AI Delegation Matrix
nodes.summary: The canonical definition of how much freedom an AI agent is granted to perform a task and make decisions. Every process, skill and template in this framework declares a delegation level. This document is the authority those declarations resolve against.

data.title: AI Delegation Matrix
data.summary: The canonical definition of how much freedom an AI agent is granted to perform a task and make decisions. Every process, skill and template in this framework declares a delegation level. This document is the authority those declarations resolve against.

nodes.label: Control Points
nodes.title: Control Points
nodes.summary: The mandatory human checkpoints in the procurement value chain, and the AI delegation ceiling permitted at each one. A control point is where an agent is structurally required to stop and hand control back to a named human role.

data.title: Control Points
data.summary: The mandatory human checkpoints in the procurement value chain, and the AI delegation ceiling permitted at each one. A control point is where an agent is structurally required to stop and hand control back to a named human role.
